title: Naturality of the module tensor restriction-extension comparison
statement: Let A and B be commutative rings in one universe and let $\rho:A\to B$ be a unital ring homomorphism. For every B-module M and A-module N there are A-linear isomorphisms $e_{M,N}:\operatorname{Res}_\rho(M\otimes_B\operatorname{Ext}_\rho N)\cong\operatorname{Res}_\rho(M)\otimes_A N$, with extension of scalars [def-weil-module-base-change] and ordinary module tensor products [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. They can be chosen natural simultaneously in both modules: for all B-linear $f:M\to M\prime$ and A-linear $g:N\to N\prime$, $e_{M\prime,N\prime}\circ\operatorname{Res}_\rho(f\otimes_B\operatorname{Ext}_\rho g)=(\operatorname{Res}_\rho f\otimes_A g)\circ e_{M,N}$. There are no flatness or nonzero hypotheses.

source.place: Tag 06Y1, proof: tensor base-change identity; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06Y1

proof.text: Give B its A-algebra structure induced by ρ and M its restricted A-action. The scalar tower identity is (ρ(a)b)m = ρ(a)(bm). Mathlib TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange A B B M N gives a B-linear equivalence M tensor_B (B tensor_A N) to M tensor_A N. Restrict that equivalence to A and bundle it as a module isomorphism. Its formula is m tensor (b tensor n) maps to (b m) tensor n; its inverse sends m tensor n to m tensor (1 tensor n). The balanced relations and inverse identities are exactly those of cancelBaseChange.

For B-linear f:M→M′ and A-linear g:N→N′, prove the naturality equality by two tensor inductions, first on the outer B-tensor and then on the inner A-tensor. Zero and addition cases follow from additivity and tensor distributivity. On m tensor (b tensor n) the two sides are (b f(m)) tensor g(n) and f(b m) tensor g(n), equal by B-linearity of f. No flatness, nonzero-ring or finiteness hypothesis is used.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_tensorRestrictExtend_module_natural
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (ρ : A →+* B) :
    ∃ e : ∀ (M : ModuleCat.{u} B) (N : ModuleCat.{u} A),
      (restrictScalars ρ).obj (M ⊗ (extendScalars ρ).obj N) ≅
        (restrictScalars ρ).obj M ⊗ N,
      ∀ (M M' : ModuleCat.{u} B) (N N' : ModuleCat.{u} A)
        (f : M ⟶ M') (g : N ⟶ N'),
        (restrictScalars ρ).map (f ⊗ₘ (extendScalars ρ).map g) ≫ (e M' N').hom =
          (e M N).hom ≫ ((restrictScalars ρ).map f ⊗ₘ g)
